commit.message:
Redesign the blog's post lists, post header and tag pages (#3500)

* Simplify the blog's post lists, metadata and tag pages

List every post on the homepage and redirect /posts/ and /archives/ to it. Replace cards with rows, drop pagination and the dot separators, remove the press animation, restyle the post description and byline, and show tags as lowercase chips everywhere.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Give the search result focus outline some room

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Give the blog one type ramp, color set and layout

The list, post, tag, search and 404 pages now draw on one set of tokens at
the top of custom.css: seven type sizes, four text colors and an accent, and
a 4px spacing scale. Every page title has the same style and position.

Header, text and footer share one 720px column. On wide screens the year,
date and reading time hang in the left margin, so post titles start on the
same edge as the page heading. Posts are separated by space alone, and the
rules around the byline and between rows are gone.

Dates and reading times are set in monospace, author names are stronger than
their roles, and the list and the post header render both through the same
partials. The list shows names only.

Geist and a subset of JetBrains Mono are served from the site, with their
licenses alongside.

The button and youtube shortcodes no longer emit a <style> block, which had
been ending up in the feeds and the search index.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Align the blog's metadata and even out spacing in posts

Dates, reading times, years and tag counts are now set in Geist like the rest
of the page. JetBrains Mono is for code only.

Whatever shares a line now shares its size and line height, so the tops line
up as well as the baselines. In the list the year and date are set like the
title beside them and the reading time like the summary. On a post the date
stands beside the author's name and the reading time beside the role.

Post bodies use three gaps: 24px between paragraphs and lists, 32px around
anything that is not running text, and 48px above an h2. They are set on
block-level boxes so they collapse. Buttons used to add their own margin on
top, and code, images, tables and quotes each had different values.

The second of two buttons is outlined, so it reads as the same size as the
filled one. "Tier 1", "July 28" and the like no longer break across lines in
titles and descriptions.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Drop the blog's accent color and finish the small controls

The indigo accent is gone, so the blog is neutral like the docs site. Links in
text are ink with a grey underline, quiet links turn ink under the pointer,
titles gain an underline, and controls get a stronger fill or outline. The
focus ring is ink. On a tag page the tag stays in ink and the words before it
step back.

The table of contents is a panel with a chevron, built like a code block, so it
reads as a control and is set apart from the text. The back-to-top link and the
carousel arrows are the same 40px outlined square as the second button, with
centered line icons.

Authors in the byline are spaced by a fixed gap and no longer by thirds of the
column. The tags under a post use the block gap and the footer has one gap on
every page.

Tables fill the column and scroll inside a wrapper when they need more room.
The copy button is level with the first line of code.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Center a post's tags between the text and the footer

The gap above the tags and the gap above the footer are now the same 48px
token. 4px comes off the first, because a line of body text keeps more room
under its baseline than the footer's small text keeps above its capitals. On
screen both distances measure 53px.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Update the Ruby SDK Tier 1 blog post (#3496)

* Update the Ruby SDK Tier 1 blog post

The post was written on September 29 and merged on October 30. Since
then SEP-3398 moved the next specification release from December 2026
to late March 2027, and the mcp gem went from 1.6.1 to 1.8.2.

Set the date to the day the post went live and rename the file to
match. Correct the release target, refresh the install and upgrade
steps, list the Tier 1 requirements, link the SEPs, state the upgrade
caveat in plain words, and use the 18 days recorded in the assessment.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Fold the upgrade command into the Gemfile step

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Reword the Tier 2 assessment sentence

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Add buttons for the Ruby SDK and its documentation

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Add spacing between adjacent blog buttons

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Say MCP spec instead of revision

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Loosen the wording of the Tier 2 assessment paragraph

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Move the credits into an Acknowledgements section

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Emphasize the two remaining Tier 1 gaps

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Reword the lead-in to the Tier 1 progress list

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* State the triage window plainly in the feedback section

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Add context, progress numbers and a roadmap link to the Ruby post

Say what Tier 1 means for Ruby developers, put numbers and a graphic
behind the Tier 3 to Tier 1 progress, and link the SDK roadmap. Drop
the bottom margin on blog buttons so the gap before the next heading
matches the rest of the page.

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Rename the Tier 2 to Tier 1 section heading

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Redraw the Ruby SDK tier progress graphic

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Revise the text of the Ruby SDK Tier 1 post

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>

* Correct the custom headers bullet and the undocumented features sentence

Co-authored-by: den <den@anthropic.com>
